claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 17 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 17 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you, I need to know about your child or children. Let me ask you the first question:

**How old is your child (or oldest child if you have more than one)?**

Please tell me:
- Your child's age, OR
- Their date of birth

This will help me determine which path through the eligibility rules applies to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old. That's very helpful.

Since Alex is 17, he falls into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, I need to check whether he's in education or training, as this affects eligibility.

Let me navigate to the next stage:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently in education or training?** 

For example:
- Attending school, college, or university (full-time or part-time)
- In an apprenticeship
- In a recognised training course

Or has he recently left education (within the last 20 weeks)?

Please let me know his current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex is still in education studying for his A-levels. That's helpful information.

Since he's in education, I need to check the specific level of education to ensure it meets the eligibility requirements:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I can see the education level requirements. Good news - **A-levels are approved education** for Child Benefit eligibility purposes.

However, I need to check a couple of things to ensure Alex meets all the requirements:

1. **Is Alex studying A-levels on a full-time basis?** (The requirement is a minimum of 12 hours per week of supervised study)

2. **Is Alex married?** (If he is, he would only qualify if he's financially dependent on you)

Please let me know about these details.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, he's studying full-time at college - he's there every weekday during term time, so definitely more than 12 hours a week.

And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex is studying A-levels full-time with well over 12 hours per week of supervised study, and he's not married. That all checks out perfectly for approved education.

Now let me navigate to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check one more thing about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or does he not have paid work at all?**

(This is asking whether he's working 23 hours per week or less, or not working at all. If he's working 24 hours or more per week, that would affect eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't work at all, so he's well under the 24-hour threshold. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check whether Alex is receiving any benefits in his own right:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits in his own name?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (as a claimant in his own right, not as a dependent)

If he's not receiving either of these, please say yes. If he is receiving one or both, please let me know.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He's still dependent on me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own name. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check whether Alex is in an apprenticeship:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

If yes, I need to know which type and where:
- England (any type of apprenticeship would disqualify)
- Scotland (Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify)
- Wales (Foundation Apprenticeships are approved, but other types would disqualify)

Or is he not in an apprenticeship at all (which it sounds like, since he's doing A-levels)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just doing his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship - he's just studying A-levels at college. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about your residency situation?** 

The main question is: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

This could also include special circumstances such as:
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Being a Crown servant living abroad
- Other specific eligibility routes

For most people, the simple answer is whether they normally live in the UK. What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK in Manchester. That meets the residency requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check whether you're responsible for Alex. Responsibility means:

**Do ANY of the following apply to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** - he lives in your household
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - you pay at least an equivalent amount to Child Benefit towards his care (this could include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. **You're paying maintenance** - you make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers his upkeep

Based on what you've told me so far (you mentioned he's your son and you're in Manchester), I'm guessing you live with Alex and support him. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me. We live together.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex lives at home with you in Manchester. That clearly establishes you're responsible for him. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important point about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any other person who might also be claiming for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also claiming for him?
- Is any grandparent or other family member claiming for him?

Or is only you claiming (or planning to claim) for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one planning to claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check whether there are any special circumstances regarding where Alex is living:

**Is Alex in any of these situations:**

1. **In hospital** - currently admitted to hospital
2. **In care** - in local authority care or foster care
3. **Fostered** - living with foster parents
4. **Normal living** - living at home with you

Based on what you've told me, I believe he's living normally at home with you. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - he's living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're nearly there. Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you fully covering his costs (or the vast majority), or is the council paying towards his housing or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything. I'm covering all his costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You're covering all of Alex's costs yourself, and the council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance.

Excellent news! Based on my assessment of your situation against the Child Benefit eligibility requirements, I can now provide you with your result:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Congratulations! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Summary of Your Situation:
- **Child:** Alex, age 17
- **Education:** Full-time A-levels at sixth form college (approved education)
- **Work:** Not working
- **Benefits:** Not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
- **Living situation:** Living at home with you in Manchester
- **Responsibility:** You are responsible for him, and no one else is claiming
- **Other factors:** Council is not paying towards his accommodation

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Important note:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay some or all of the benefit back through tax

### Payment Details:
- Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if applicable in your circumstances)
- Current rates: Check gov.uk for the latest Child Benefit payment amounts

### Useful References:
- How to claim: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- General information: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

He meets all the key requirements: he is within the eligible age range, in approved full-time education (A-levels), not working full-time, not receiving conflicting benefits, you are responsible for him living in the UK, and there are no disqualifying factors such as council funding or other claimants."
